But the narrative has a factual mismatch about the cited claims, and the cited examples and next steps are generic, so an investigator would need to redo some work.","problems":["Narrative says C0190858, C0190898, C0190900 'carry only symptom codes such as rash or upper respiratory infection'; the card shows R21 (rash), J06.9 (URI) and R21, so this is roughly right, but C0190858 and C0190900 are both R21 only, and the 'upper respiratory' example fits only C0190898 – minor imprecision.","Claim that the 99215 excess 'appears across every complexity tier' is only loosely supported: tier shares are all above the provider-wide baseline, but the 3-condition tier has n=1 and the 4 and 5+ tiers are tiny, so it is thin evidence.","The 'Examples' cited in the structured section (C0190815, C0190837) differ from those discussed in the narrative (C0190858, C0190898, C0190900) and are not the strongest low-complexity examples; osteoarthritis and hyperlipidemia are chronic conditions, and 0-condition cases would be more telling.","Next steps are generic: 'request a larger sample of 99214 and 99215 claims' and 're-screen' name no specific claims, although the narrative suggests requesting charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims. The next steps do not match the narrative.","Does not note that one documented supported 99215 (C0190883) has minutes 'not recorded', or that the low-complexity claim C0190964 (heart failure) is only borderline low complexity, which weakens the 'low-complexity but supported' counterpoint.","The note-inflation statement 'little sign of inflated notes' rests on 1 of 11 and a tiny sample, which is slightly over-interpreted."]}
